spec.speciesBlurb: What your character is. Sets size, speed, senses, and a handful of traits that follow you at every level.
spec.speciesOptionBlurb: The branch of {species} you belong to — it layers its own traits on top.
spec.backgroundBlurb: What your character did before adventuring. Two skills, a tool, a language — and in 5.5e the ability boosts. It works in a scene, not in a fight.
spec.classBlurb: What your character does. Hit die, saving throws, the skill list you choose from, and every feature that arrives with a level.
spec.classReplaceBlurb: This row is {class}. Picking here replaces it rather than adding a class — for a second class, use “Multiclass” on the sheet.
spec.subclassBlurb: The specialisation inside {class}. It adds features at its own levels.
spec.featBlurb: This level offers one improvement: raise your abilities, or take a feat that does something an ability score cannot.
spec.abilitiesBlurb: The six numbers everything else is built from. Pick how they are generated, then allocate — every boost that lands on them is listed underneath.
spec.skillsBlurb: Your class offers a list to choose from; your background grants its own for free. Expertise doubles proficiency on a skill you already have.
spec.languagesBlurb: What your character can speak and read.
spec.spellsBlurb: Cantrips are always ready; leveled spells start prepared and can be re-prepared in the Spellbook after a rest.
spec.inventoryBlurb: What your character carries. Equipping armour, a shield, or a weapon changes AC and your attacks immediately.
spec.notesBlurb: Bonds, flaws, whatever the table needs to remember. Goes to your GM; it changes nothing on the sheet.
spec.originFeatBlurb: Your background grants this feat outright — it is not picked and cannot be cleared. What is left here is what the feat asks you.

demo.title: Heads up — this demo only ships the free SRD content
demo.body: Charnik is in active development. We can only include the SRD — the part Wizards of the Coast released for free (CC-BY). The rest of D&D belongs to them, not us, so a lot of it legally can't be here out of the box: Artificer, Aasimar, the Beholder, most subclasses, and loads of spells & monsters. But nothing holds you back — make your own homebrew and, with the flexible CSV system, add whatever you want: from species and classes to spells. You can also download the full desktop app for your computer — it keeps all your data local and needs no internet connection.
demo.readonly: Editing isn't available in the demo. Download the desktop app to save changes.

packs.title: Content updates
packs.desc: Content packs are folders of CSVs — the shipped SRD is simply the one Charnik bundles. Charnik can check whether a pack’s repository has newer rules data, so a correction reaches you without a new app version. Only GitHub repository links work for now. Checking is one request per repository per day at most; APPLYING an update is always your click.
packs.desktopOnly: Content updates are a desktop feature — the web demo always serves the content of its own deploy.
packs.chipTitle: {count, plural, one {# content pack has} other {# content packs have}} newer rules data. Open Settings to see what would change.
packs.none: No content packs are registered yet.
packs.filesPreserved: {count} file(s) you edited will be kept as they are
packs.rowsRemoved: {count} entries would DISAPPEAR from your content
packs.draftsAffected: Unfinished edits that would be left with nothing to edit: {who}
packs.packTooLarge: “{pack}” is too big to download: {files} files, {mb} MB (limit {maxFiles} files, {maxMb} MB).
packs.carriesPlugins: This pack also contains plugins: {list}. They arrive switched off and need your review.
packs.changesPlugins: This update rewrites plugin code: {list}. Applying it stops those plugins until you approve the new code, and any stats they calculate will change.
packs.installGone: “{pack}” is no longer among the packs Charnik found in that repository — the listing it was offered from has moved on. Check for updates again, then install it from the fresh list. Nothing was changed.
packs.applyGone: There is no longer an update waiting for “{pack}” — it was already applied, or a newer check found it had been withdrawn. Nothing was changed.
packs.applyBadRepo: Charnik can no longer tell where “{pack}” comes from, so it has nothing to download from. Its recorded link is {repo}. Remove the pack’s repository and add it again. Nothing was changed.
packs.hostUnsupported: Charnik can’t check {repo} — update checks currently work with GitHub repository links only.
packs.tooManyPacks: {repo} offers {packs} content packs — more than Charnik will list at once (limit {max}). Nothing was changed; a repository this large is more likely a mistake in the link than a collection you meant to browse.
packs.repoTooBig: {repo} holds too many files for GitHub to list in one go, so Charnik only ever sees part of it — and acting on half a list could delete content that is still there. Nothing was changed.
packs.sourceChanged: “{pack}” now claims to be a different source (“{from}” → “{to}”). That makes it a NEW pack, not an update: every entry would be renamed and any character using them would lose the link. Nothing was changed — install it as a separate pack instead.
packs.sourceClaimed: “{pack}” publishes its entries as “{source}” — the same name “{owner}” already uses here. That name is what the app shows as an entry’s origin, so this pack’s entries would look like they came from “{owner}”, and the two would share one on/off switch. That’s normal for a fork of the same content, and a red flag for anything else. Nothing was installed.
packs.saveFailed: Charnik couldn’t save your content-pack settings. Pins, repository links and the update mode are still in force for now, but they will be gone when you close the app — and a pinned pack could then be updated. This is almost always the data folder being full, read-only, or on a drive that has gone away: check it, then flip any pack setting to try saving again. ({message})
packs.noPacksFound: No content packs found in {repo} — a pack is a top-level folder holding CSV files.
packs.nameTaken: The folder “{name}” already belongs to another pack, so this one goes in a folder of its own. Change the name if you like.
packs.folderTaken: The folder “{name}” is already in use — pick another name.
packs.badFolderName: “{name}” can’t be used as a folder name.
packs.renameBundled: “{name}” is one of the packs the app ships, so it keeps its folder — that is how the app knows to keep it up to date and to offer it back if you delete it.
packs.readyOffline: Downloaded and ready — applying it works offline
packs.ownRepoHint: Charnik’s own packs — the SRD ones it ships with — live at
packs.missingLabel: Deleted, but still in the app
packs.missingNote: Not on your disk. The copy inside the app can go back any time — no internet needed.
packs.contentMoved: “{path}” changed on the server while it was being downloaded. Nothing was written; check again in a moment.
packs.localChanged: These files changed on your disk after this update was prepared: {files}. Nothing was written, because the summary you approved no longer describes them. Check for updates again to see the current picture.
packs.rowsWouldVanish: This update deletes {count, plural, one {# entry} other {# entries}} from inside the files it rewrites. Nothing was written yet — check the list below, then apply again to accept it.
packs.undoDone: “{pack}” is back to the version it had before the last update.
packs.uninstallWarn: Deletes its files from your disk, and the {count} entries it gives you with them. Characters using any of those go blank there. You can get it back any time from {repo}.
packs.uninstallWarnEmpty: Deletes its files from your disk. Characters using anything from it go blank there. You can get it back any time from {repo}.
